'''''Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi''''' is a [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series from [[Dark Horse Comics]], written by [[John Ostrander]] and pencilled by [[Jan Duursema]], the creative team behind Dark Horse's critically-acclaimed ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' series. ''Dawn of the Jedi'' is set almost 26,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], and the series focuses on the [[Je'daii Order]], a group of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] who are the predecessors to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Aside from the beginning of the [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|first issue]], ''Dawn of the Jedi'' is primarily set in the year [[25,793 BBY]], in a time before the polarization of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and the series is the first to be set "[[Before the Republic]]"—a new publishing era that includes all material set before the founding of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

A preview [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0|Issue 0]] was released on [[February 1]], [[2012]], and it was followed by the series' first issue on [[February 15]]. Not a monthly series, ''Dawn of the Jedi'' released fifteen issues as part of three five-issue story arcs, [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm|''Force Storm'']], [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan|''The Prisoner of Bogan'']], and [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force War|''Force War'']]. The series focuses on three young [[Je'daii Journeyer]]s—[[Shae Koda]], [[Tasha Ryo]], and [[Sek'nos Rath]]—as well as [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]], a [[Force Hound]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] who recently arrived on Tython, and the mad Je'daii [[Daegen Lok]]'s plans to take over the Je'daii Order. ''Force War'' focuses on the Infinite Empire's arrival and attempted conquest of the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]]. ''Dawn of the Jedi'' ended after the third arc, as [[Marvel Comics]] acquired the ''[[Star Wars]]'' comic publishing license from Dark Horse in [[2015]].
